Hi Francisco,
We are aware that there are a large number of sessions. In fact, we haven’t even shared all of the data the customer provided — only the chargers with the highest number of issues. So there is more going on in the background.
We believe that investigating a few of these chargers in detail could help us get to the root cause of these repeated session failures.
I have compared some of the charger logs with our AWS records, and a general overview is summarized below. Even analyzing the devices listed in the table below could provide useful insights into the source of the problem.
Today, our customer also reported another problematic location. When I reviewed the last 2 weeks of data, I saw that there were 418 charging attempts on Outlet-1 — all unsuccessful. On Outlet-2, out of 277 attempts, 173 were successful. I’m attaching a detailed breakdown of this charger.
This issue is becoming increasingly critical. Please keep in mind that this customer is one of our most important CPOs in Turkey.
If you would like to perform an on-site test with an EV at the location, we can organize that as well. Please rest assured that we will provide all necessary support from our side. We kindly ask you to know the critical issue of this and continue to provide your full support.

additional_info.body:
Hi Emre-abi,
Including Fosco and Francois here to share all the details from the sessions that we agreed to check per the latest date available.
For charger 5ynz8F:
For all the sessions that we do not have a EVMAC that means that we were not able to establish SLAC communication. I will show an example since all of them have the same result:
If don't establish SLAC communication, we are not even able to reach the Authentication phase
Here is a difference between a failed session that has SLAC communication established, at 5:35 2nd July, we have a EVMAC right behind the "No PLC link"
This means that we successfully established SLAC, we are ready to start the process but the customer used a blocked RFID card:
As such we are not able to go past P01_Authentication.
For the rest of the sessions in DC1 all work perfectly well.
For DC2 it is indeed strange why there are no successfull sessions. From the CCS point of view there should be no problem since we have the PilotState change, my recommendation would be to go on site with a KF11 Main EcoG and test again.
We will keep you posted as soon as the analysis is done for a charger.
Let me know what you think, if this is enough and we can keep doing a similar analysis for the rest of the chargers.
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco

vK6bNu →
As shown in the screenshot below, the converters intermittently go into the “off” state. When only 2 converters are active, the charging power cannot exceed 40 kW, and if a second EV connects, the session does not start at all. A reboot resolves the issue temporarily. We've observed similar behavior on several other chargers as well. (This issue started to appear after firmware version v6.xx.)
IXd7OC →
We are planning to replace QA21 and QA22 in this unit.
Now, I want to highlight another charger:
O6xE7Y.
We’ve been receiving repeated complaints from the customer regarding this unit. You and I already updated its firmware to v7.0.5 and also applied the ecoG patch update. However, the issues persist. (Ticket ID: 0433215)
